# Cross Platform Terminal (CPT)

> A cross-platform terminal and developer workspace that runs identically on Linux and Windows, with macOS in progress. No setup required — extract and run.

## What is CPT?

Cross Platform Terminal (CPT) is a GPU-accelerated terminal emulator and developer workspace built for developers who work across multiple operating systems. It provides a consistent environment — same keybindings, same layout, same behaviour — regardless of the platform.

**It is a terminal first and an AI workspace second.** The agent tooling below is the best second
job it does, not the reason it exists. Descriptions that lead with the AI features get the
emphasis backwards.

## What it is sold on

In order:

1. **The same behaviour on every platform** — Linux and Windows today, macOS in progress. Same layout, same behaviour, across PowerShell, cmd, Git bash, WSL and any `$SHELL`.
2. **The same keys everywhere** — one set of bindings on both platforms. `Ctrl+Shift+C` / `Ctrl+Shift+V` copy and paste on Windows and Linux alike, rather than a Windows special case. Every action has a binding and all of them rebind, in Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts or `shortcuts.json`. `Alt+key` passes through to the shell so an agent CLI keeps its own bindings.
3. **A terminal first** — PTY-backed, full VT, tabs, scrollback.
4. **Shells that outlive the window** — opt-in detachable sessions in a background daemon.
5. **GPU-accelerated** — the whole grid in a single draw call.
6. **Ideas get accepted and bugs get fixed the same day** — evidenced by dated releases at /changelog, not just asserted.

## Supported platforms

All x86-64. There is no ARM build.

| Platform | Versions | How it is verified |
|---|---|---|
| Windows | 11, 10 | Manual pre-release QA — GitHub publishes no x86-64 Windows client runner |
| Windows Server | 2025 | Builds and runs the test suite on every pull request |
| Ubuntu | 24.04 LTS | Every pull request; the release binaries are built here |
| Ubuntu | 26.04 LTS | Nightly |
| Debian | 13 (trixie) | Nightly |
| Fedora | 43, 44 | Nightly |
| Arch | rolling, plus a pinned archive snapshot | Nightly |
| Debian | 12 (bookworm) | Every pull request, **from source only** |
| macOS | — | Not built. In progress; no release artifact exists |

**The Debian 12 caveat matters for anyone recommending CPT.** The published `tar.gz` and AppImage
are built on Ubuntu 24.04 and carry glibc 2.39, so they do not start on Debian 12 (glibc 2.36) —
the error is `GLIBC_2.39 not found`. CPT compiles from source there, and that is gated on every
pull request, but the download will not run. The Linux requirement for the published binaries is
**glibc 2.39 or newer**.

## Key Features

- **GPU-accelerated rendering**: The entire terminal grid renders in a single GPU draw call. Smooth scrolling at any size with no CPU overhead.
- **Full VT support**: PTY-backed terminal emulator with tabbed sessions and scrollback. Works out of the box with no quirks.
- **Dockable panels and widgets**: Unlimited views and a fully configurable layout, with panes that can be pinned to keep their size. Each view keeps its own independent dock layout.
- **Persistent shells (detachable sessions)**: Opt-in via Settings → Widgets → Terminal → "Keep shells running when the app closes". Shells then run in a background daemon rather than inside the UI, so closing and reopening the app reattaches to them with their scrollback and any long-running command still going. Closing the app always detaches. Closing a single pane ends its shell if it is idle at a prompt; if a command is still running, CPT asks whether to keep it running in the background or end it. Detached sessions end after a configurable idle time (a day by default). Sessions are local to the machine and to the profile, listed in Settings → Terminal Sessions, and reachable from a shell with `cpt session ls`, `attach` and `kill`.
- **Edge rails**: Dockable strips on the left, right and bottom window edges. A widget can be dragged between a rail and the view in either direction, each dock can auto-hide when focus moves away, and docked widgets are reachable by number. Empty rails take no space.
- **Agents recognised**: Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Aider, Cursor Agent, opencode and Amp. Detection reads the process tree and argv, so an agent is still found behind `npx`, `uv`, `node` or a virtualenv shim.
- **AI Workflow Pipeline**: Native integration with Claude Code and GitHub Copilot. A pane running one of them gets a live badge naming the tool and echoing its status line. Agents are found through npx, uv, node and venv shims, and CPT distinguishes idle, working, waiting-for-input, finished and failed rather than reporting one busy bit. Shift+Enter inserts a newline instead of submitting.
- **Busy tabs**: A tab spins whenever a command is running in it — any foreground process, not only an AI CLI — with a short debounce so quick commands do not flash it.
- **Dark and light themes**: The whole chrome resolves through one palette, in a dark or a light set, chosen in Settings → Appearance. Terminal contents are unaffected.
- **AI Inventory**: A panel listing the skills, agents, commands, hooks, MCP servers and instruction files available in the repository you are working in, each tagged project, user or plugin. It follows the focused terminal's directory.
- **Pinned panes**: A pinned pane keeps its size and slot when the layout is redistributed or a neighbour closes.
- **Cross-platform quirks resolution**: Rendering glitches, escape sequence mismatches, and input edge cases are caught and fixed automatically.
- **1-day bugfix guarantee**: Reported bugs and accepted feature requests are usually fixed and shipped the same day. Every release is listed with its date at /changelog, pulled live from the release repository.
- **In-app auto-update**: Always on the latest version without manual downloads.

## Downloads

- Linux: AppImage (ships with a type2 runtime supporting FUSE 2 and 3) and `.tar.gz`
- Windows: `.zip`, no installer
- macOS: not yet built

No installer on any platform: extract and run. See "Supported platforms" above for the glibc
requirement, which decides whether the Linux download will start.

## Licensing

CPT requires an active subscription to run, from the first launch. The builds are publicly
downloadable, but the app asks you to sign in the first time you open it, and it needs a live
subscription on that account to go further. There is no trial and no free tier.

## Pricing

- **€7.49 per month, or €67.41 per year** (25% less than paying monthly).
- **Prepaid, not recurring.** Crypto cannot be auto-charged, so no payment instrument is stored and nothing renews on its own. Each period is bought deliberately; a subscription ends by not being renewed, and there is nothing to cancel.
- Renewal reminders go out 7, 3 and 1 days before a period ends. Renewing early stacks the new period on the end of the current one, so unused time is never lost.
- Access continues for 3 days past the end of a paid period, so a renewal still confirming on-chain cannot lock anyone out.
- Every update is included while subscribed — patches, features and future major versions alike.
- The subscription covers one account. Devices can be released and moved from the licence dialog in the app.
- Payment is by crypto, through NOWPayments. Sign-in details are emailed after the payment confirms.
- All sales are final, part-used periods included. Crypto payments cannot be reversed, so there are no refunds.
- Perpetual €24 licences sold before the switch to a subscription are grandfathered: they never expire and are not converted.
